name: Light Mallow Purple
lede: Light Mallow Purple is a bright pink-purple named for the mallow flower, recorded by Ridgway in 1912 and classed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955 as a deep purplish pink.

sections.title: A flower, not a pigment
sections.body:
Our data files the name under mallow, the flower, rather than a pigment or a place [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate XII at hue 67, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same area as block 248, "deep purplish pink" [1]. In LCH terms it reads as lightness 69, chroma 50, hue 337 degrees: bright and strongly saturated, close to magenta [1].

Its nearest computed neighbors are [[lavender-pink|Lavender Pink]], 4.0 units off, and [[persian-pink|Persian Pink]] and [[orchid-crayola|Orchid (Crayola)]], both a little duller [2]. The closest everyday name is [[orchid]], about 7.8 units away [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our 23,781-painting archive has no painting where a close match covers at least one percent of the canvas, as photographed; that describes this archive, not painting as a whole [4]. Our data groups the name under "magenta" for naming purposes, alongside its sibling [[light-hortense-violet|Light Hortense Violet]] [5].
